title: Testing with XCTest and Swift Testing

videos.script: A test is a small program that states what your code must do, and complains when it does not. {{xctest}} The older framework first, XCTest. A class, methods whose names start with test, and an assertion that compares two values. Its first run finds a week with minus thirty minutes left. {{testing}} Then Swift Testing, which arrived in 2024. One check, expect, that takes an ordinary expression, and prints every value inside it when it fails. It finds a percentage that is always zero, and the cause is lesson 1's integer division. {{cases}} Then one test run with many inputs, and an edge case that forces a decision. {{async}} Then code that waits. An async test simply awaits it, and never sleeps. {{doubles}} Then stand-ins for a server: one that works, one that is always offline, one that fails halfway and counts. {{running}} And last, choosing which tests run, and what a coverage number does not tell you. By the end, the planner's library has ten tests in two frameworks, and you can read both.
